title: Magikarp's Seven-Foot Jump Has One Wild Exception

direction.premise: Magikarp's rare jumps usually stop at seven feet, but one Pokédex entry gives an absurd exception.
direction.audiencePromise: Follow the seven-foot clue until Magikarp's age unlocks a mountain-sized reveal.
direction.openLoop: How can a Pokémon with a seven-foot jump limit clear a mountain?
direction.payoff: A Magikarp living many years can leap a mountain using Splash, even though the move remains useless.
direction.engagementQuestion: Seven-foot cap or mountain leap: which feels more like Magikarp?

voice.instructions: Quick, warm, and playful. Stress seven feet, many years, and mountain. Pause briefly before each reveal, then land the final choice clearly.

scenes.headline: SEVEN FEET. THEN A MOUNTAIN.
scenes.narration: Magikarp's jump stops at seven feet—unless it ages.
scenes.caption: A STRICT JUMP LIMIT… OR MORE?

scenes.headline: THE POKÉDEX SETS A CAP
scenes.narration: Some entries cap its rare jumps at seven feet.
scenes.caption: RARE JUMPS HAVE A LIMIT

scenes.headline: THE RULE GETS STRANGER
scenes.narration: That sounds final, until one entry makes it much stranger.
scenes.caption: THE LIMIT ISN'T THE WHOLE STORY

scenes.headline: AGE UNLOCKS THE MOUNTAIN
scenes.narration: A Magikarp living many years can leap a mountain using Splash.
scenes.caption: MANY YEARS → MOUNTAIN LEAP

scenes.headline: THE MOVE IS STILL USELESS
scenes.narration: The same entry calls Splash useless, even after that mountain leap.
scenes.caption: MOUNTAIN LEAP. USELESS MOVE.

scenes.headline: WHICH MAGIKARP DO YOU BELIEVE?
scenes.narration: Seven-foot cap or mountain leap: which feels more like Magikarp?
scenes.caption: SEVEN FEET OR MOUNTAIN?
